newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat futures settle mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat futures settle mostly higher.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled mostly higher on a mix of commercial pricing and short covering by locals and funds, traders said.
"We saw scale-down buying early in the July. It was commercial pricing, I think, but also there was some fund buying," a MGE floor source said.
Nearby July spring wheat was also buoyed by reports of a lack of movement in North Dakota due to dry weather.
"It's pretty dry in North Dakota and a lot of farmers are holdiing on to their old crop wheat out of hope that the dry weather might force the price back up," a trader said.
Traders said MGE spring wheat lost ground relative to KCBT wheat on intermarket spreading.
MGE spring wheat settled 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 3-1/4 cents higher, with July up 3-1/4 cents at $3.89-1/4. New crop September gained two cents to close at $3.84-1/2.
Traders said Cargill Investor Services, Atwood-Peavey and Linnco Futures had each bought at least 500,000 July bushels.
